reason: E2 directly supports the premise that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves room-temperature ductility in RHEAs, but the cited evidence provides no support for the other key premises regarding Ti addition to NbMoTaW, irradiation tolerance, high-temperature strength retention, or mitigation of amorphization/blistering.
premises: Adding Ti to NbMoTaW will form a dual-phase BCC + B2 microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
An 'inverted' BCC + B2 microstructure (discrete B2 in BCC matrix) improves room-temperature compressive ductility in RHEAs.
The B2 precipitates and their interfaces will act as effective defect sinks, enhancing irradiation tolerance.
The modified alloy will retain high-temperature strength comparable to single-phase BCC NbMoTaW.
The intervention will mitigate irradiation-induced amorphization and blistering.
